title: Sensory Regeneration Following Abdominoplasty in Massive Weight Loss Patients and Its Impact on Sexual Function and Quality of Life
summary: Following abdominoplasty – a surgical procedure to remove excess skin after significant weight loss – many patients report persistent sensory disturbances in the abdominal area, such as numbness or altered sensation. How the sense of feeling recovers in the long term and whether this is linked to sexual satisfaction and body perception has so far been poorly investigated. This study invites patients who underwent abdominoplasty at BG Klinik Tübingen between 2010 and 2025 following significant weight loss to attend a single examination appointment of approximately four hours. During this appointment, abdominal sensation is assessed using standardised warm, cold, and pressure stimuli, and skin perfusion, elasticity, and tissue thickness are measured. In addition, participants complete questionnaires on quality of life, body image, and sexual satisfaction. For comparison, individuals who have also lost significant weight but have not undergone abdominoplasty will be examined as well.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Study Group – Inclusion Criteria:
Abdominoplasty (standard horizontal or fleur-de-lis technique) between 2010 and 2025 at BG Klinik Tübingen, massive weight loss ≥ 20 kg (post-bariatric or conservative), minimum age 18 years at time of surgery, at least 6 months postoperatively at time of examination, capacity to consent, sufficient knowledge of German.

Control Group – Inclusion Criteria:
Massive weight loss ≥ 20 kg (post-bariatric or conservative), clinically documented excess skin of the abdomen, minimum age 18 years, written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Study Group – Exclusion Criteria:
Less than 6 months postoperatively, circular abdominoplasty/lower body lift/360° techniques, previous abdominoplasty or abdominal wall revision, history of laparotomy with midline incision, history of caesarean section, major abdominal surgery with abdominal wall dissection, revision with re-dissection more than 2 weeks after primary surgery, acute wound healing disorders at time of examination, manifest peripheral neuropathy, systemic neurological disorders (multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease), chronic pain syndrome with long-term analgesic use, acute skin infections in the measurement area, severe chronic skin disorders in the examination area, pregnancy, severe psychiatric disorders, lacking capacity to consent or withdrawal of consent, insufficient knowledge of German.

Control Group – Exclusion Criteria:
Previous abdominal surgery with potential influence on abdominal wall sensation (e.g. caesarean section, laparotomy), neurological disorders affecting peripheral sensory function, active skin disorders in the examination area, pregnancy or breastfeeding, lacking ability to cooperate for examination.
